project.name: Paja
project.summary: Paja is Kehto's local workshop for building napplets (small sandboxed web apps that talk to a host over the NIP-5D protocol). A command-line dev server serves a host page; in the browser that page loads a napplet into a locked-down iframe and wires it to the real Kehto runtime, shell, firewall and reference services so the napplet behaves as it would in a production host.

nodes.label: Command line and dev server
nodes.summary: The `kehto paja` command: reads flags and settings files, optionally starts the napplet's own dev command, waits for it, and serves the host page plus a pinned resource proxy on a local port.

nodes.label: Options and simulation
nodes.summary: Shared rules both halves agree on: launch options and settings files, the simulated identity/relay/storage setup, multiplayer settings checks, and which NAP domains Paja advertises.

nodes.label: Browser host app
nodes.summary: Everything bundled into browser-host.js: the page that frames napplets, connects them to Kehto, asks the user for approvals, and shows the developer panels.

nodes.label: Host bootstrap and tabs
nodes.summary: Starts the page, builds the shell bridge, keeps one tab per loaded napplet, and restores tabs after a reload.

nodes.label: Napplet loading
nodes.summary: Turns a dev-server URL, a dropped HTML file or a Nostr napplet pointer into verified bytes, then places them in a sandboxed iframe and binds its NIP-5D identity.

nodes.label: Kehto wiring
nodes.summary: Builds the shell adapter that plugs every NAP domain into @kehto/services handlers, scoped to the napplet window that asked.

nodes.label: Firewall, signers and consent
nodes.summary: Firewall approval prompts and default rules, grant revocation, signer choice (built-in dev key or remote NIP-46 signer) and remembered signing consent.

nodes.label: Relays and social lookups
nodes.summary: Connects to live Nostr relays (or an in-memory stand-in), picks relays per request, and keeps saved copies of profiles and contact lists.

nodes.label: Files, uploads and resources
nodes.summary: Blossom uploads and blob addresses, the per-napplet file system, and resource fetching for network-isolated napplets.

nodes.label: Realtime and CVM
nodes.summary: WebRTC rooms, multiplayer identity, and ContextVM (Nostr-carried tool server) discovery.

nodes.label: LLM connections
nodes.summary: Lets the developer add model provider connections, keeps their keys in a password-locked vault, and serves NAP-LLM requests.

nodes.label: Intents and installed napplets
nodes.summary: Builds and opens shareable intent links, keeps the catalog of installed napplets, and launches the napplet that handles an intent.

nodes.label: Sidebar sections and dev panels
nodes.summary: The collapsible sidebar sections for resource servers, CVM discovery and the nested-frame lock, plus the developer console, message log, relay panel and gamepad indicators.

nodes.label: Tests
nodes.summary: Automatic checks for every area, including command-line parsing, relay behaviour, firewall prompts, intent links and the sidebar settings sections.

nodes.label: @kehto/runtime
nodes.summary: Kehto's protocol engine: message dispatch, permissions and subscription lifecycle.

nodes.label: @kehto/shell
nodes.summary: Browser adapter: ShellBridge, iframe policy, approval UI.

nodes.label: @kehto/services
nodes.summary: Reference handlers for each NAP domain (relay pool, storage, upload, DM, CVM, LLM...).

nodes.label: @kehto/firewall and limits
nodes.summary: Firewall rule evaluation, permission principals, and caps on how often a napplet may ask.

nodes.label: @kehto/nip
nodes.summary: NIP-5A/5D napplet resolution and NIP-65 relay lists.

nodes.label: @napplet core and nostr-tools
nodes.summary: Protocol types, NAP contracts and Nostr event helpers.

nodes.label: Model providers
nodes.summary: Outside model services a developer connects, such as OpenAI.

edges.label: serves browser-host.js
edges.description: The host page HTML loads the separately bundled /__kehto/browser-host.js and passes it the host config as JSON.

annotations.note: ~1,000-line bootstrap that wires every controller; the single place the ShellBridge, firewall adapter, sidebar settings sections and intent links are created.

steps.note: `kehto paja --target-url …` parses options, may spawn the dev command, and waits until the target answers.
Starts the local server, probes the target's CORS, and plans whether it runs live or as an isolated snapshot.
Renders the host page with the config and frame policy, and points it at browser-host.js.
In the browser: creates the adapter and ShellBridge, then opens a tab for the target or a pasted pointer.
For a Nostr pointer, fetches the manifest from relays, verifies the bytes and adds a strict CSP.
Navigates a fresh sandboxed iframe via srcdoc and registers its identity with the shell.
Forwards the napplet's one-time hello to the bridge, which binds its MessagePort; NAP traffic then flows.
A napplet calls a NAP operation; the adapter routes it to the matching Kehto service.
The runtime sees the napplet lacks a grant for that scope and asks the permission adapter.
Paja's adapter checks the default rules first; only 'ask' results become a prompt.
Default rules allow everything except opening external links, which always asks.
The shell's approval UI shows the prompt; the decision is stored as a grant and the call proceeds or fails.
On page load, the host reads the address for a Paja intent link and checks its size and fields without running it.
The link controller opens the shared content straight away, asking the recipient to pick an app only when more than one fits.
Works out which verified napplet the link names or the user prefers, from the installed-napplet catalog, under normal pointer checks.
Creates a hidden, sandboxed launcher frame and registers it with the shell like any other napplet.
Verifies Paja's signed launcher napplet and posts the link only to that registered frame, which raises the intent over NAP-INTENT.
Opens or focuses the napplet that handles the intent and queues one delivery to it once it is ready.

tour.title: Start with the command
tour.note: Developers run `kehto paja` from their napplet's package. It starts their dev server if asked and serves Paja's host page locally.

tour.title: Shared rules
tour.note: Launch options, settings files, the simulated user and relays, and which NAP domains are advertised live here so the server and the page agree.

tour.title: The page in the browser
tour.note: The host page frames each napplet in a sandboxed iframe and connects it to Kehto.

tour.title: Wiring Kehto packages
tour.note: The adapter is where Paja plugs @kehto/runtime, @kehto/shell and @kehto/services together for every NAP domain.

tour.title: Approvals and signers
tour.note: Firewall prompts, default rules and signing consent keep a napplet from acting without the developer's say-so.
